body: Wednesday, November 29 2023 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information available before 2023-11-29 00:00 UTC. Prices use completed prior sessions. Prepared retrospectively; later outcomes are excluded.

Macro Stance: Mixed: disinflation is winning the argument, but markets have already paid for most of the good news. Fed Governor Waller said he is confident inflation is headed back to 2 percent  [1] , while Bank of America says interest-rate cuts are coming next year  [2] . When a sitting governor sounds that confident, the market stops debating one more hike and starts debating the date of the first cut, which is exactly the shift visible at the front of the curve. Demand is cooling at the margin rather than breaking: Black Friday online spending set a record $9.8 billion, up 7.5%  [3] , yet Reuters cited a report showing the softest Black Friday-week sales gain in years even as discounts drew the crowds  [4] . Record dollars bought with markdowns is the profile of a consumer still spending but trading down, which supports bonds more cleanly than higher equity multiples.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y Treasury closed at 4.73% and the 10Y at 4.34% (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-28), leaving 10Y-2Y at -39 bps and 10Y-3M at -113 bps, so the curve shape remains inverted. Over 20 observations the 2Y fell -30 bps from 5.03% and the 10Y fell -54 bps from 4.88%, a bull flattening in which the 10Y-2Y spread moved a further -24 bps. The last five observations look different at the front: the 2Y dropped -16 bps against -8 bps for the 10Y, the policy-sensitive end repricing cut odds rather than reacting to growth. The 3M bill at 5.47% shows the funds rate has not moved, so every basis point of easing is still an expectation. Supply is the counterweight: $7.6 trillion of US government debt matures within a year  [5] , and Semafor's 'nobody wants U.S. Treasury bonds' framing  [6]  is the risk to the duration trade if auctions start to tail.

New / Most Important: The dollar is on pace for its worst month of 2023 on bets the Fed is done raising rates  [7] ; DXY closed at 102.75, -3.18% over 20 sessions from 106.12 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28). Easier financial conditions show up everywhere, yet index momentum has stalled: the S&P 500 sits at 4,554.89, +9.31% over 20 sessions but only +0.17% over five, VIX has collapsed to 12.69, down 7.06 points in 20 sessions, and the Russell 2000 is -0.79% over five sessions at 1,792.81. Sell-side optimism is escalating anyway, with Deutsche Bank now predicting a record 5,100 for the S&P 500 in 2024  [8] .

Playbook ✓: Own intermediate duration through IEF (93.38 USD, +4.01% over 20 sessions) rather than the long bond, because the rally is anchored in policy expectations at the front and belly. Keep S&P 500 exposure at benchmark and use VIX at 12.69 to buy cheap downside protection instead of adding beta into a stalled tape. Trigger to extend duration: a 2Y break below 4.73% on a softer core inflation print. What changes the call: a 10Y retracing toward 4.88%, the level 20 observations ago, or a dollar rebound that undoes the DXY's -3.18% month.

Macro Stance: Mixed. The euro area is stagnating while its equity markets ride lower global yields. Germany's economy shrank slightly in the third quarter  [9] , and its economic challenges are complicating resolution of the budget crisis despite the chancellor's reassurances  [10] . The region's largest economy is therefore contracting at the moment its fiscal room is being questioned, which removes the natural stabiliser for a weak 2024 and leaves the ECB as the only macro lever, and the ECB is still talking tough.

Activity & Inflation: Activity data stay soft: the euro zone's October PMI sat near a three-year low, stirring recession worries  [11] . The ECB warns that banks are starting to show stress as loan defaults rise  [12] , while Governor De Cos calls it premature to talk about rate cuts  [13] . That is a central bank holding the line in words while credit quality erodes underneath. It usually ends with policy following the data, and in the meantime European duration benefits from every further fall in US yields.

New / Most Important: The currency is doing some of the tightening: the euro has hit three-month highs while the dollar faces its weakest month in a year  [14] . Corporate Europe is restructuring into it, with Volkswagen cutting headcount at a core brand it calls 'no longer competitive'  [15] . The Euro Stoxx 50 closed at 4,348.02, +7.06% over 20 sessions, and the DAX at 15,992.67, +7.98% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28), while the dollar-priced FEZ is +11.37%, a reminder that much of the euro-area rally seen from abroad is currency translation.

Playbook ✓: Hold European equity exposure through quality industrial and software names with pricing power, such as Siemens (+21.17% over 20 sessions) and SAP (+12.47%), and stay light on credit-sensitive domestic lenders while the ECB's default warnings build. Trigger to add: PMIs turning up from the October trough. What changes the call: a further euro surge that squeezes exporters' margins, or a German budget fix that restores fiscal impulse.

Macro Stance: Bearish. Beijing is signalling support without the scale that would change the growth trajectory. The PBOC governor pledged to support growth while urging reforms  [16] , a pairing that usually signals targeted relending and structural tools rather than broad household transfers. Industrial profit growth slowed, keeping stimulus calls alive  [17] , so the private sector is asking for more than the central bank is offering. The policy mix is supply-side: credit to factories, piecemeal property easing and administrative support for share prices. That combination lifts output and exports before it lifts domestic prices or margins, which is why we stay underweight broad China beta and pick single names instead.

PMIs & Activity: A Reuters poll expects November factory activity to have contracted for a second month  [18] , so the pending official PMI is expected to confirm rather than reverse the October slump. Trade data tell the same story from the outside: exports fell for a sixth straight month in October while imports rose  [19] . Rising imports alongside falling exports is more consistent with input stockpiling than with a consumer recovery. The pattern is a producer economy running ahead of its customers: volumes hold, prices give. For equity investors that means volume-led earnings with little pricing power, a poor mix for cyclical margins and a reason to expect further downgrades in materials and industrial exporters before upgrades arrive.

Credit Impulse: Credit is flowing, but to the wrong end of the economy for a demand recovery. Reuters reports that a surge in high-tech manufacturing loans is raising fears of a wave of cheap exports  [20] , a supply impulse that pressures global goods prices rather than reflating China. At the household end, shadow finance is cracking: a Chinese shadow bank admitted a £30bn shortfall after 'management ran wild'  [21] , the kind of loss on savings products that makes households more cautious, not less. Directed lending to factories plus losses in savings products is a combination that raises the saving rate at exactly the wrong moment. Until credit shows up in household borrowing and mortgage demand, the impulse supports industrial volumes more than consumer equities.

Property: Property policy is loosening city by city. Shenzhen cut down payments on second homes as cities try to revive demand  [22] , and China is weighing unprecedented builder support through first-ever unsecured loans  [23] . Buyers have not responded: more Chinese cities recorded falling home prices in October  [24] . Unsecured developer lending keeps projects alive and protects suppliers, but it socialises losses onto bank balance sheets rather than restoring buyer confidence, which is the variable that matters for sales. The signal to watch is second-home easing spreading to the other tier-one cities; until then, falling prices keep households in wait-and-see mode and the property drag on growth persists into 2024.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Technology controls still bite even as the diplomatic tone softens. Nvidia shares closed lower on a report it delayed a China AI chip designed to comply with US export rules  [25] , which means Chinese cloud buyers face both delay and capability limits on imported accelerators. That pushes spending toward domestic suppliers and away from US vendors, a slow structural loss for the latter. Western capital is recalibrating as well: Goldman Sachs is paring back its 'growth at all costs' China strategy  [26] , a sign that the investment-banking fee pool from Chinese listings and cross-border deals is not expected to rebuild quickly. For markets, the trade and technology channel matters more right now than any fiscal headline.

Markets & Flows: Onshore equities are being propped rather than bid. Reuters reports the Beijing bourse told 'major shareholders' to refrain from selling  [27] , administrative support that limits downside but rarely creates sustained upside. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,038.55, +0.66% over 20 sessions, while the Hang Seng ended at 17,354.14, -2.14% over five sessions, and FXI lost -3.67% over the same five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28). Dispersion is extreme: PDD jumped +18.08% in a single session and Tencent is +10.51% over 20 sessions, but Alibaba in Hong Kong is -7.12% over 20 sessions and Baidu's ADR fell -3.52% on Tuesday. Offshore money is picking winners, not buying the index, and the onshore market is being held up by regulators rather than by buyers.

New / Most Important: Two capital-markets signals stand out. Shein has filed for a US IPO in a major test of investor appetite  [28] , and Meituan launched a $1 bln share buyback  [29] ; Chinese consumer platforms are monetising through US listings and buybacks rather than waiting for a domestic re-rating. Huawei is pushing its technology into the EV world with new cars and automaker partnerships  [30] , a competitive threat that matters as much to foreign carmakers as to Chinese rivals. Corporate China is adapting to slow growth with capital returns and export ambition, which helps selected stocks but does not fix the macro.

Playbook ✓: Stay underweight broad China beta through FXI and the Hang Seng; express any long only through cash-returning platforms such as Tencent and PDD, or through iron-ore exposure listed outside China. Trigger to cover the underweight: an official PMI back above 50 together with tier-one property easing and evidence of household credit growth. What deepens it: renewed home-price declines or a failed listing window for the Shein deal. ⚠ Divergence: policy is visibly easing, through PBOC pledges, Shenzhen's down-payment cut and exchange guidance against selling, while the data keep deteriorating, with factory activity expected to contract again and home prices still falling; the market is trading the policy, not the data.

Macro Stance: Mixed. Japan finally has the inflation it spent decades wanting, and Reuters reports investors are tearing up their old playbooks around it  [31] . Japanese inflation data were upbeat even as the dollar-yen pair traded sideways  [32] , and Oxford Economics expects 2024 wage rises to look as high as this year's  [33] , the wage-price loop that would let the BOJ normalise. The policy debate is about timing, not direction. The market has not yet forced it: the Nikkei 225 closed at 33,408.39, +7.80% over 20 sessions but just +0.06% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28), and EWJ is +7.38% over 20 sessions in dollar terms.

Activity & Currency: The weak yen is the transmission channel. Singapore travellers are splurging in Japan amid a weakening yen  [34] , which flatters tourism and exporters' translated profits while squeezing household real incomes through import prices. Governance is the stronger equity story: Toyota group companies plan a $4.7 billion sale of a Denso stake  [35] , the kind of cross-shareholding unwind that can release capital for buybacks and lift return on equity. That gives foreign investors a reason to own Japan without a strong currency view, since buybacks raise per-share earnings whatever the yen does. In semiconductors, Tokyo Electron is +21.83% over 20 sessions and Advantest +12.66%, while Toyota trails at 2,755.00 JPY, +4.42%, and Sony sits at 12,825.00 JPY, +5.82%.

Playbook ✓: Stay long Japan through governance and chip-equipment winners such as Tokyo Electron and Advantest rather than export-heavy autos, because yen weakness is already in prices and any BOJ normalisation would hit currency-driven earnings first. Trigger to add: wage settlements consistent with the Oxford Economics view and the Nikkei 225 holding above 33,408.39. Hedge part of the currency exposure, since a stronger yen would erode dollar returns on unhedged holdings. What changes the call: a sharp yen rebound on a policy shift, which would favour domestic-demand names over exporters.

Macro Stance: Mixed, leaning hawkish. RBA Governor Bullock says inflation is increasingly homegrown, suggesting rates will remain high  [36] , and argues households are coping even as Lowe issues a warning  [37] . Consumers are waiting for discounts: October retail sales slipped as shoppers held off for Black Friday  [38] , a timing effect that could flatter the next print and complicates the RBA's read. A central bank that sees inflation as homegrown has little reason to ease just because goods prices cool, so the hold is likely to be long even if the next hike never comes.

Demand & Financing: Housing is where demand and financing collide. Experts warn a temporary pull-back in migration might be necessary to relieve rental stress  [39] , because population growth is outrunning supply and rents feed directly into homegrown inflation. The external side offers an offset: analysts see iron ore at $150 in 2024 on Chinese stimulus  [40] , and the Aussie dollar has hit a three-month high  [41] . The ASX 200 closed at 7,015.20, +3.46% over 20 sessions, lagging global peers because banks and miners dominate the index and neither benefits much from falling US yields, with BHP at 46.43 AUD and Commonwealth Bank at 103.34 AUD, +7.02% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28).

Playbook ✓: Prefer Australian banks over miners while homegrown inflation keeps the cash rate high, since net interest margins benefit from a hawkish hold. Trigger to rotate into BHP and Fortescue: a Chinese PMI back above 50 with iron ore confirming the stimulus call. What changes the call: a domestic inflation undershoot that revives cut expectations and compresses bank margins.

Macro Stance: Bullish. Poland is the rare European economy where real incomes, credit and confidence are all turning up together. GDP is growing again for the first time in two quarters as the economy 'bounces off the bottom'  [42] , and Super Biznes reports the first rise in consumption in 9 months  [43] . Wages are rising 'like yeast', which Analizy.pl expects to strengthen consumption  [44] : with nominal pay outpacing prices, households regain purchasing power and the recovery becomes consumption-led rather than export-led, which suits domestic banks and retailers. Ipsos finds consumer confidence back near pre-pandemic levels  [45] , so households are willing to spend the gains rather than save them. The constraint is that October inflation came in higher than first estimated  [46] , which limits the room for further monetary easing and keeps real rates from falling much further.

Markets: Polish equities have been one of the month's strongest trades. EPOL closed at 22.32 USD, +2.53% on the day and +13.13% over 20 sessions, while the Beta ETF WIG20TR tracker is +5.23% over 20 sessions at 40.47 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); much of the gap between the dollar-priced fund and the zloty-priced tracker reflects the currency contribution. Banks led Tuesday's session, with mBank +3.28%, PKO Bank Polski +2.00% and Pekao +1.76%, while KGHM rose +2.13% to 117.40 PLN, tracking the global metals bid rather than domestic politics. Business Insider Polska writes that the Polish currency 'shines' globally and forecasts still give the zloty room  [47] , yet Bankier's currency survey finds analysts unconvinced by an 'era of a strong zloty'  [48] . Credit is re-accelerating: mortgage sales are sharply higher on 'government steroids', a quarter 'like the good old days'  [49] , which feeds bank volumes but also housing demand.

Fiscal & Politics: Politics is in an awkward interregnum that markets are choosing to look through. OKO.press calls the newly sworn Morawiecki cabinet a government for two weeks that will fall after 14 days  [50] , and Gazeta Prawna says it has no chance of a confidence vote and no budget  [51] . The 2024 budget that matters will instead be submitted by Donald Tusk's government  [52] , so the fiscal plan investors must price is the new coalition's, whose full cabinet list is already circulating  [53] . The fiscal prize is EU money: the European Commission accepted Poland's revised KPO recovery plan, with energy the biggest winner  [54] . Tusk's flagship pledge to raise pay  [55]  is the spending risk bond investors will price once the new team takes office; a pay rise funded by EU inflows is benign, one funded by extra issuance is not.

Corporate & Sectors: The KPO approval, with energy named the biggest winner, coincides with a sharp utility rally: PGE is +16.90% over five sessions at 8.45 PLN and Tauron +12.65% at 4.23 PLN. PGE also adds a nuclear leg, as PGE PAK Energia Jądrowa received the decision-in-principle for a KHNP plant in Wielkopolska  [56] . CD Projekt earned over 200 mln zł of net profit in Q3  [57] , yet the stock closed -1.51% at 107.95 PLN and is -4.64% over five sessions, so the print lands on a share that has been de-rating into it. Budimex won a Czech D11 motorway contract worth 2 mld zł  [58] , a sign that Polish contractors can export capacity while domestic tenders wait for EU money. Retail is split, with Pepco +30.36% over 20 sessions and Dino +13.79% at 444.00 PLN while Allegro is -2.20%, so the consumer recovery is being priced in discount and food retail rather than in e-commerce. JSW is the casualty at -18.27% over five sessions, with Wyborcza reporting that prosecutors slowed a probe into money siphoned out of the coal miner  [59] .

Geopolitics & Security: Security spending is structural, not cyclical. Rzeczpospolita reports Poland is building an air shield worth 54 mld zł that will also protect its Patriot batteries  [60] . The threat is concrete: Poland charged 16 people after dismantling a Russian spy ring  [61] , evidence that the war's spillover risk now extends inside Poland's borders. The Ukrainian relationship also carries economic friction, as Polish truckers started a round-the-clock blockade of a fourth border crossing  [62] . For investors the blockade is a logistics and trade-flow risk for exporters and transport names, while defence outlays are a multi-year commitment that a change of government is unlikely to reverse.

New / Most Important: The NBP has become a political battleground. A new NBP banner no longer argues that inflation is gone; it now says Governor Glapiński is 'the best'  [63] . Rzeczpospolita reports the NBP pays millions to Glapiński's advisers and will not disclose their names  [64] , the kind of disclosure fight that invites scrutiny from the incoming coalition. The bank is also publicly rebutting accusations that its bond purchases were unconstitutional  [65] , a defence suggesting the bank expects scrutiny under a new government. For markets the risk is credibility rather than the policy rate: a central bank in open conflict with the incoming government can widen the risk premium on Polish bonds and the currency even as the fundamentals improve.

Playbook ✓: Stay long Polish equities through EPOL and the WIG20TR tracker, overweight banks (PKO, Pekao, mBank) and KPO-linked utilities (PGE, Tauron), sized for headline volatility around the NBP and for legal risk after the Supreme Court voided a loan agreement over a bank's FX tables  [66] . Trigger to add: a clean confidence vote for the Tusk cabinet and a 2024 budget that funds the pay pledge without a jump in issuance. What changes the call: a confrontation that threatens NBP independence or a stall in KPO disbursement. ⚠ Divergence: the macro and currency signals are unambiguously positive, but the institutions are in open conflict, with a caretaker cabinet lacking a majority and a central bank campaigning for its own governor, so the political risk premium could rise just as growth improves.

Narrative: Platform software is carrying the AI trade while hardware gets scrutinised. XLK closed at 184.75 USD, +13.45% over 20 sessions but -0.38% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Microsoft is +13.46% and Adobe +18.29% over the same 20 sessions, while Apple trails at 190.40 USD.

Reported: HPE projected sales that fall short of estimates on server demand  [67] , a reminder that the AI build-out is not lifting every hardware vendor, as budgets appear to shift from general-purpose servers to accelerators. Apple is trying to unwind its Goldman Sachs credit-card partnership  [68] , trimming a low-margin financial-services experiment rather than adding one.

EPS Upside Watch: Cloud distribution is widening: Amazon will offer Salesforce apps on AWS, allowing easier integration of AI tech  [69] . Marketplaces that bundle software with compute shorten sales cycles, which is where upside to 2024 software revenue estimates is most likely to appear, especially for vendors whose pricing scales with usage rather than seats.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Consensus treats AI as a chip story; the better risk-reward now sits in software with usage-based pricing, where server-cycle shortfalls like HPE's do not bite. Stay Bullish, but fund it from hardware rather than adding net exposure while the sector consolidates its 20-session gain.

Narrative: Communication services have rallied on lower yields, but the news flow is about liability, not growth. XLC closed at 70.69 USD, +9.78% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Meta is +12.00%, Alphabet +10.24% and Netflix +16.81%, while Disney fell -2.81% in Tuesday's session.

Reported: States claim Meta deliberately targeted young users and ensnared them with addictive technology  [70] , litigation that targets product design rather than a single practice. At X, the NYT reports up to $75 million of revenue at risk as more advertisers pull out  [71] .

EPS Upside Watch: Advertising budgets leaving X have to land somewhere, and the largest, most measurable platforms tend to capture them; that is the near-term upside case for Meta and Alphabet ad revenue into the holiday quarter. Netflix's +16.81% month shows investors still pay for subscription pricing power.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The market prices regulatory risk at Meta as a fine-sized cost. The underappreciated threat is product redesign: if child-safety litigation forces changes to recommendation algorithms, engagement and ad load fall together, and that hits margins far harder than any settlement. Mixed until the legal path clarifies.

Narrative: Financials are the cleanest beneficiary of a soft landing with lower long yields. XLF closed at 35.25 USD, +10.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Bank of America is +14.95%, JPMorgan +11.73%, and the regional-bank KRE +11.81% despite a -2.33% five-session pullback.

Reported: Bank of America pays a $12 mln fine for misreporting mortgage data  [72] , a cost of doing business rather than a franchise risk. Its +14.95% month suggests investors care far more about the securities book than about conduct fines of that size.

EPS Upside Watch: Consolidation is the upside catalyst: KBW has named the regional banks at greatest risk of being taken over by rivals  [73] . Takeover premia matter because acquirers with excess capital can buy deposit franchises below replacement cost when regional valuations are depressed, and the bid itself re-rates the rest of the group.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Investors still treat falling yields as bad for bank margins. For banks carrying underwater securities, lower long yields shrink unrealised losses and free capital faster than they compress net interest income. Stay Bullish, with large money-centre names ahead of regionals.

Narrative: Energy is the one sector that has gone nowhere, -0.31% over 20 sessions at 84.65 USD for XLE (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28), because crude has slid: Brent sits at 81.68 USD/bbl, -6.56% over 20 sessions, WTI at 76.41 USD/bbl, -7.17%, and Henry Hub gas -24.31% to 2.71 USD/MMBtu.

Reported: Oil fell 4% when OPEC delayed its meeting  [74] , and an OPEC source told Reuters that bigger cuts are a likely option  [75] , consistent with Brent's +2.13% session. The cartel is signalling, not yet acting.

EPS Upside Watch: Downstream and gas exposure are the swing factors for estimates. Exxon is -1.87% over 20 sessions and SLB -7.25%, so services already discount weaker activity; integrated majors with refining and chemicals can hold earnings even if crude stays near current levels, while gas-weighted producers face estimate cuts after the month's collapse.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Consensus frames the OPEC decision as binary. The bigger signal is natural gas: a -24.31% month is disinflation that helps consumers and industrial users more than it hurts the integrated majors. Mixed, with a bias to integrated balance sheets over pure upstream.

Narrative: Industrials are splitting between aerospace strength and farm-machinery weakness. XLI closed at 105.49 USD, +8.04% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Boeing is +21.95% over the same period while Deere is -5.34% over five sessions.

Reported: Deere shares tumbled after its 2024 guidance missed estimates  [76] , suggesting the farm-equipment cycle may have peaked. Caterpillar, at 247.50 USD and +2.21% over 20 sessions, shows construction equipment holding up better than farm machinery.

EPS Upside Watch: Order books are the upside driver: Airbus and Boeing are poised for a major Thai Airways widebody order  [77] . Widebody demand supports engine and aftermarket earnings well into 2024, which is where estimate revisions tend to follow; Boeing's +21.95% month says the market is starting to price that recovery.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Investors still price industrials off the manufacturing PMI. The better guide is backlog quality: aerospace backlogs are long-dated and price-protected, while ag equipment is exposed to farm incomes. Stay Bullish on aerospace, avoid machinery tied to the farm cycle until dealer inventories and order books stabilise.

Narrative: Consumer discretionary has priced a strong holiday. XLY closed at 169.48 USD, +12.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Amazon is +10.79% and Home Depot +11.32%, while Lululemon slipped -1.82% in Tuesday's session. Home Depot's month more likely reflects falling mortgage-rate expectations than holiday spending.

Reported: Cyber Monday sales hit a record $12.4 billion even as savings dwindle  [78] , and Amazon called its Black Friday and Cyber Monday event its 'biggest ever'  [79] . Headline volumes are strong, but the savings cushion behind them is thinning, which makes them harder to repeat.

EPS Upside Watch: Scale is the margin lever: the biggest platforms can fund promotions from advertising and logistics income, while specialty retailers fund them from gross margin. That asymmetry is where fourth-quarter EPS surprises will separate, favouring Amazon over discount-dependent chains.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The market reads record holiday spending as bullish. The more relevant number is margin: promotional intensity transfers value from retailers to shoppers. Favour scale platforms over discount-dependent specialty retail, and watch full-price brands such as Nike and Lululemon as the test of that thesis. Mixed for the sector as a whole.

Narrative: Staples are catching a defensive bid as yields fall but face a structural demand question. XLP closed at 70.53 USD, +1.57% over five sessions and +4.30% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Walmart is -2.69% over 20 sessions, while Costco is +7.05% at 594.00 USD.

Reported: Morgan Stanley has identified the stocks with the most at risk as patients on Ozempic eat less  [80] , and Berkshire Hathaway sold its entire Procter & Gamble stake  [81] , a notable vote from a long-term staples owner.

EPS Upside Watch: Pricing power is fading as goods inflation cools, so volume has to do the work. The upside case is value retail: warehouse clubs gain share as shoppers trade down, consistent with Costco outpacing Walmart over the month. Branded food faces the opposite mix, with slowing price increases and a structural volume question from appetite-suppressing drugs.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The consensus treats GLP-1 drugs as a niche risk for snacks. If adoption broadens, the volume hit spreads to beverages and packaged food, and defensive multiples no longer look defensive. Mixed, with a preference for value retail over branded food.

Narrative: Health care is the laggard of the rally, XLV +4.69% over 20 sessions at 129.64 USD and -0.51% on Tuesday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28). Eli Lilly is at 591.60 USD, Novo Nordisk's ADR fell -2.35%, and Pfizer is -2.82% over 20 sessions, while Intuitive Surgical is +20.29%.

Reported: A data analysis found Lilly's Mounjaro leads to more and faster weight loss than Novo's obesity drug  [82] . The FDA is investigating the safety risk of CAR-T cancer therapies  [83] , a regulatory overhang for cell-therapy developers.

EPS Upside Watch: Obesity remains the clearest estimate-revision story in large-cap pharma: head-to-head efficacy data shift prescribing at the margin, and supply capacity determines who captures the demand. Lilly's ability to convert its efficacy edge into volume is the upside case, while post-Covid franchises like Pfizer keep resetting lower.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Investors still treat pharma as one defensive block. The real trade is dispersion: obesity leaders versus post-Covid decliners, and device makers such as Intuitive Surgical, whose +20.29% month suggests procedure volumes are holding up. Mixed for the sector, Bullish on obesity share-gainers and cautious on Covid-exposed franchises.

Narrative: Materials are turning on a weaker dollar and steadier metals. XLB closed at 81.18 USD, +7.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Freeport-McMoRan is +9.34%, Newmont +10.97% over five sessions, copper +4.38% over 20 sessions to 3.80 USD/lb and gold +1.92% over five to 2,040.00 USD/oz.

Reported: The Northern Miner expects gold and silver to rise as political and economic risks grind on  [84] , and the tape agrees: Freeport-McMoRan rose +1.72% on Tuesday and the copper-miner ETF COPX +2.15%, while Alcoa slipped -0.84%, so the bid favours copper and gold over aluminium.

EPS Upside Watch: Silver's +5.73% over five sessions shows the precious-metals bid is broadening beyond gold. Historical Analog: The mechanism is operating leverage. A miner's costs, mostly power and machines, are largely fixed in the short run, so revenue above break-even drops almost straight to profit; that is why miner shares tend to move several times as much as bitcoin in both directions. The same leverage makes them the first casualties when the coin stalls, and miners often fund expansion by selling new shares into rallies, which caps the upside for existing holders. The crowd remembers the upside half of that mechanism; warnings such as Yahoo Finance's argument that Coinbase's valuation is getting ahead of itself  [111]  are a reminder the other half exists.

Smart Money View: Standard Chartered is the institutional bull in this story, with its year-end 2024 target of $100K  [100] . The other side is made up of regulators and critics. The third is the target itself. A bank forecast is not a flow, and a year-end 2024 number  [112]  is a long way from a miner's next power bill. MARA's 8.85 USD level 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28) shows how much of the run is borrowed from the future.

Where It Breaks: The miners' jump is leverage to the metal, and leverage cuts both ways. Reuters reported gold dropping below $2,000 only last week as the dollar gained and yields pared losses  [95] , so a single hawkish voice could do it again. CBS's roundup of what experts think about gold prices in 2024  [122]  shows how mainstream the bet has become, and a consensus that broad tends to crack on the first surprise. A close back below 1,994.30 USD/oz, gold's level 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28), would say the Fed-is-done trade is priced.

Why Retail Is Here: The meme trade got its obituary and a pulse on the same day. Reuters says Roundhill will shut its MEME ETF due to flagging investor interest  [104] , yet GameStop jumped 13.27% to 13.49 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28). The crowd's story is defiance: every time the establishment declares the meme era over, the original meme stock reminds everyone it can still squeeze. The defiance is selective, though. AMC, the other icon, fell 1.47% and is down 32.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28), so the energy is concentrated in one ticker rather than a revival of the whole movement.

Where It Breaks: Flagging interest is the base rate, and Roundhill's decision  [104]  is the market's own verdict on how many buyers remain. A one-day pop that rests on short covering rather than news tends to fade as fast as it came, and the business underneath is still a game retailer; Kotaku's first-person account of a GameStop Black Friday deal from hell  [123]  is not a growth story. GameStop is up only 5.39% over 20 sessions from 12.80 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); a slide back below that level would confirm the pop was a squeeze, not a turn.

Why Retail Is Here: The value crowd lost one of its two patron saints. Barron's asks what Charlie Munger's death means for Berkshire Hathaway and its stock  [109] , and the tributes are already circulating as investing scripture: Yahoo Finance compiled 44 memorable Munger quotes about life and markets  [124] , and Money Digest reports where Munger saw the stock market going in 2024  [125] . Berkshire's B shares slipped 0.36% to 360.05 USD and remain up 6.71% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28). For Buffett followers, owning Berkshire is a vote of faith in the people as much as the businesses.

Where It Breaks: That faith premium is exactly what succession tests. Business Insider reminds readers how much Berkshire has lagged tech stocks over the last 20 years  [126] , and says Munger made investing mistakes too  [127] , so the case for owning the shares has to rest on the businesses rather than the legend. If tributes give way to questions about who allocates the capital next, the stock's 337.41 USD level 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28) is where faith turns into a discount.

geo.label: Fed on hold, cuts being priced
parts: Macro Stance

Mixed: disinflation is winning the argument, but markets have already paid for most of the good news. Fed Governor Waller said he is confident inflation is headed back to 2 percent [[n1782]], while Bank of America says interest-rate cuts are coming next year [[n1815]]. When a sitting governor sounds that confident, the market stops debating one more hike and starts debating the date of the first cut, which is exactly the shift visible at the front of the curve. Demand is cooling at the margin rather than breaking: Black Friday online spending set a record $9.8 billion, up 7.5% [[n0117]], yet Reuters cited a report showing the softest Black Friday-week sales gain in years even as discounts drew the crowds [[n1780]]. Record dollars bought with markdowns is the profile of a consumer still spending but trading down, which supports bonds more cleanly than higher equity multiples.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y Treasury closed at 4.73% and the 10Y at 4.34% (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-28), leaving 10Y-2Y at -39 bps and 10Y-3M at -113 bps, so the curve shape remains inverted. Over 20 observations the 2Y fell -30 bps from 5.03% and the 10Y fell -54 bps from 4.88%, a bull flattening in which the 10Y-2Y spread moved a further -24 bps. The last five observations look different at the front: the 2Y dropped -16 bps against -8 bps for the 10Y, the policy-sensitive end repricing cut odds rather than reacting to growth. The 3M bill at 5.47% shows the funds rate has not moved, so every basis point of easing is still an expectation. Supply is the counterweight: $7.6 trillion of US government debt matures within a year [[n0120]], and Semafor's 'nobody wants U.S. Treasury bonds' framing [[n1825]] is the risk to the duration trade if auctions start to tail.
New / Most Important

The dollar is on pace for its worst month of 2023 on bets the Fed is done raising rates [[n1818]]; DXY closed at 102.75, -3.18% over 20 sessions from 106.12 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28). Easier financial conditions show up everywhere, yet index momentum has stalled: the S&P 500 sits at 4,554.89, +9.31% over 20 sessions but only +0.17% over five, VIX has collapsed to 12.69, down 7.06 points in 20 sessions, and the Russell 2000 is -0.79% over five sessions at 1,792.81. Sell-side optimism is escalating anyway, with Deutsche Bank now predicting a record 5,100 for the S&P 500 in 2024 [[n0749]].
Playbook ✓

Own intermediate duration through IEF (93.38 USD, +4.01% over 20 sessions) rather than the long bond, because the rally is anchored in policy expectations at the front and belly. Keep S&P 500 exposure at benchmark and use VIX at 12.69 to buy cheap downside protection instead of adding beta into a stalled tape. Trigger to extend duration: a 2Y break below 4.73% on a softer core inflation print. What changes the call: a 10Y retracing toward 4.88%, the level 20 observations ago, or a dollar rebound that undoes the DXY's -3.18% month.

geo.label: ECB on hold, euro tightening
parts: Macro Stance

Mixed. The euro area is stagnating while its equity markets ride lower global yields. Germany's economy shrank slightly in the third quarter [[n1010]], and its economic challenges are complicating resolution of the budget crisis despite the chancellor's reassurances [[n1042]]. The region's largest economy is therefore contracting at the moment its fiscal room is being questioned, which removes the natural stabiliser for a weak 2024 and leaves the ECB as the only macro lever, and the ECB is still talking tough.
Activity & Inflation

Activity data stay soft: the euro zone's October PMI sat near a three-year low, stirring recession worries [[n0968]]. The ECB warns that banks are starting to show stress as loan defaults rise [[n1001]], while Governor De Cos calls it premature to talk about rate cuts [[n0996]]. That is a central bank holding the line in words while credit quality erodes underneath. It usually ends with policy following the data, and in the meantime European duration benefits from every further fall in US yields.
New / Most Important

The currency is doing some of the tightening: the euro has hit three-month highs while the dollar faces its weakest month in a year [[n1043]]. Corporate Europe is restructuring into it, with Volkswagen cutting headcount at a core brand it calls 'no longer competitive' [[n0614]]. The Euro Stoxx 50 closed at 4,348.02, +7.06% over 20 sessions, and the DAX at 15,992.67, +7.98% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28), while the dollar-priced FEZ is +11.37%, a reminder that much of the euro-area rally seen from abroad is currency translation.
Playbook ✓

Hold European equity exposure through quality industrial and software names with pricing power, such as Siemens (+21.17% over 20 sessions) and SAP (+12.47%), and stay light on credit-sensitive domestic lenders while the ECB's default warnings build. Trigger to add: PMIs turning up from the October trough. What changes the call: a further euro surge that squeezes exporters' margins, or a German budget fix that restores fiscal impulse.

geo.label: Targeted easing, no bazooka
parts: Macro Stance

Bearish. Beijing is signalling support without the scale that would change the growth trajectory. The PBOC governor pledged to support growth while urging reforms [[n0209]], a pairing that usually signals targeted relending and structural tools rather than broad household transfers. Industrial profit growth slowed, keeping stimulus calls alive [[n0202]], so the private sector is asking for more than the central bank is offering. The policy mix is supply-side: credit to factories, piecemeal property easing and administrative support for share prices. That combination lifts output and exports before it lifts domestic prices or margins, which is why we stay underweight broad China beta and pick single names instead.
PMIs & Activity

A Reuters poll expects November factory activity to have contracted for a second month [[n0229]], so the pending official PMI is expected to confirm rather than reverse the October slump. Trade data tell the same story from the outside: exports fell for a sixth straight month in October while imports rose [[n0156]]. Rising imports alongside falling exports is more consistent with input stockpiling than with a consumer recovery. The pattern is a producer economy running ahead of its customers: volumes hold, prices give. For equity investors that means volume-led earnings with little pricing power, a poor mix for cyclical margins and a reason to expect further downgrades in materials and industrial exporters before upgrades arrive.
Credit Impulse

Credit is flowing, but to the wrong end of the economy for a demand recovery. Reuters reports that a surge in high-tech manufacturing loans is raising fears of a wave of cheap exports [[n0158]], a supply impulse that pressures global goods prices rather than reflating China. At the household end, shadow finance is cracking: a Chinese shadow bank admitted a £30bn shortfall after 'management ran wild' [[n0187]], the kind of loss on savings products that makes households more cautious, not less. Directed lending to factories plus losses in savings products is a combination that raises the saving rate at exactly the wrong moment. Until credit shows up in household borrowing and mortgage demand, the impulse supports industrial volumes more than consumer equities.
Property

Property policy is loosening city by city. Shenzhen cut down payments on second homes as cities try to revive demand [[n0192]], and China is weighing unprecedented builder support through first-ever unsecured loans [[n0186]]. Buyers have not responded: more Chinese cities recorded falling home prices in October [[n0164]]. Unsecured developer lending keeps projects alive and protects suppliers, but it socialises losses onto bank balance sheets rather than restoring buyer confidence, which is the variable that matters for sales. The signal to watch is second-home easing spreading to the other tier-one cities; until then, falling prices keep households in wait-and-see mode and the property drag on growth persists into 2024.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Technology controls still bite even as the diplomatic tone softens. Nvidia shares closed lower on a report it delayed a China AI chip designed to comply with US export rules [[n0196]], which means Chinese cloud buyers face both delay and capability limits on imported accelerators. That pushes spending toward domestic suppliers and away from US vendors, a slow structural loss for the latter. Western capital is recalibrating as well: Goldman Sachs is paring back its 'growth at all costs' China strategy [[n0693]], a sign that the investment-banking fee pool from Chinese listings and cross-border deals is not expected to rebuild quickly. For markets, the trade and technology channel matters more right now than any fiscal headline.
Markets & Flows

Onshore equities are being propped rather than bid. Reuters reports the Beijing bourse told 'major shareholders' to refrain from selling [[n0215]], administrative support that limits downside but rarely creates sustained upside. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,038.55, +0.66% over 20 sessions, while the Hang Seng ended at 17,354.14, -2.14% over five sessions, and FXI lost -3.67% over the same five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28). Dispersion is extreme: PDD jumped +18.08% in a single session and Tencent is +10.51% over 20 sessions, but Alibaba in Hong Kong is -7.12% over 20 sessions and Baidu's ADR fell -3.52% on Tuesday. Offshore money is picking winners, not buying the index, and the onshore market is being held up by regulators rather than by buyers.
New / Most Important

Two capital-markets signals stand out. Shein has filed for a US IPO in a major test of investor appetite [[n0673]], and Meituan launched a $1 bln share buyback [[n0672]]; Chinese consumer platforms are monetising through US listings and buybacks rather than waiting for a domestic re-rating. Huawei is pushing its technology into the EV world with new cars and automaker partnerships [[n0232]], a competitive threat that matters as much to foreign carmakers as to Chinese rivals. Corporate China is adapting to slow growth with capital returns and export ambition, which helps selected stocks but does not fix the macro.
Playbook ✓

Stay underweight broad China beta through FXI and the Hang Seng; express any long only through cash-returning platforms such as Tencent and PDD, or through iron-ore exposure listed outside China. Trigger to cover the underweight: an official PMI back above 50 together with tier-one property easing and evidence of household credit growth. What deepens it: renewed home-price declines or a failed listing window for the Shein deal. ⚠ Divergence: policy is visibly easing, through PBOC pledges, Shenzhen's down-payment cut and exchange guidance against selling, while the data keep deteriorating, with factory activity expected to contract again and home prices still falling; the market is trading the policy, not the data.

geo.label: Reflation, BOJ patient
parts: Macro Stance

Mixed. Japan finally has the inflation it spent decades wanting, and Reuters reports investors are tearing up their old playbooks around it [[n1128]]. Japanese inflation data were upbeat even as the dollar-yen pair traded sideways [[n1156]], and Oxford Economics expects 2024 wage rises to look as high as this year's [[n1166]], the wage-price loop that would let the BOJ normalise. The policy debate is about timing, not direction. The market has not yet forced it: the Nikkei 225 closed at 33,408.39, +7.80% over 20 sessions but just +0.06% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28), and EWJ is +7.38% over 20 sessions in dollar terms.
Activity & Currency

The weak yen is the transmission channel. Singapore travellers are splurging in Japan amid a weakening yen [[n1147]], which flatters tourism and exporters' translated profits while squeezing household real incomes through import prices. Governance is the stronger equity story: Toyota group companies plan a $4.7 billion sale of a Denso stake [[n0687]], the kind of cross-shareholding unwind that can release capital for buybacks and lift return on equity. That gives foreign investors a reason to own Japan without a strong currency view, since buybacks raise per-share earnings whatever the yen does. In semiconductors, Tokyo Electron is +21.83% over 20 sessions and Advantest +12.66%, while Toyota trails at 2,755.00 JPY, +4.42%, and Sony sits at 12,825.00 JPY, +5.82%.
Playbook ✓

Stay long Japan through governance and chip-equipment winners such as Tokyo Electron and Advantest rather than export-heavy autos, because yen weakness is already in prices and any BOJ normalisation would hit currency-driven earnings first. Trigger to add: wage settlements consistent with the Oxford Economics view and the Nikkei 225 holding above 33,408.39. Hedge part of the currency exposure, since a stronger yen would erode dollar returns on unhedged holdings. What changes the call: a sharp yen rebound on a policy shift, which would favour domestic-demand names over exporters.

geo.label: RBA hawkish hold, homegrown inflation
parts: Macro Stance

Mixed, leaning hawkish. RBA Governor Bullock says inflation is increasingly homegrown, suggesting rates will remain high [[n0045]], and argues households are coping even as Lowe issues a warning [[n0086]]. Consumers are waiting for discounts: October retail sales slipped as shoppers held off for Black Friday [[n0072]], a timing effect that could flatter the next print and complicates the RBA's read. A central bank that sees inflation as homegrown has little reason to ease just because goods prices cool, so the hold is likely to be long even if the next hike never comes.
Demand & Financing

Housing is where demand and financing collide. Experts warn a temporary pull-back in migration might be necessary to relieve rental stress [[n0082]], because population growth is outrunning supply and rents feed directly into homegrown inflation. The external side offers an offset: analysts see iron ore at $150 in 2024 on Chinese stimulus [[n0089]], and the Aussie dollar has hit a three-month high [[n0084]]. The ASX 200 closed at 7,015.20, +3.46% over 20 sessions, lagging global peers because banks and miners dominate the index and neither benefits much from falling US yields, with BHP at 46.43 AUD and Commonwealth Bank at 103.34 AUD, +7.02% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28).
Playbook ✓

Prefer Australian banks over miners while homegrown inflation keeps the cash rate high, since net interest margins benefit from a hawkish hold. Trigger to rotate into BHP and Fortescue: a Chinese PMI back above 50 with iron ore confirming the stimulus call. What changes the call: a domestic inflation undershoot that revives cut expectations and compresses bank margins.

geo.label: Recovery meets caretaker politics
parts: Macro Stance

Bullish. Poland is the rare European economy where real incomes, credit and confidence are all turning up together. GDP is growing again for the first time in two quarters as the economy 'bounces off the bottom' [[n1209]], and Super Biznes reports the first rise in consumption in 9 months [[n1241]]. Wages are rising 'like yeast', which Analizy.pl expects to strengthen consumption [[n1222]]: with nominal pay outpacing prices, households regain purchasing power and the recovery becomes consumption-led rather than export-led, which suits domestic banks and retailers. Ipsos finds consumer confidence back near pre-pandemic levels [[n1188]], so households are willing to spend the gains rather than save them. The constraint is that October inflation came in higher than first estimated [[n1218]], which limits the room for further monetary easing and keeps real rates from falling much further.
Markets

Polish equities have been one of the month's strongest trades. EPOL closed at 22.32 USD, +2.53% on the day and +13.13% over 20 sessions, while the Beta ETF WIG20TR tracker is +5.23% over 20 sessions at 40.47 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); much of the gap between the dollar-priced fund and the zloty-priced tracker reflects the currency contribution. Banks led Tuesday's session, with mBank +3.28%, PKO Bank Polski +2.00% and Pekao +1.76%, while KGHM rose +2.13% to 117.40 PLN, tracking the global metals bid rather than domestic politics. Business Insider Polska writes that the Polish currency 'shines' globally and forecasts still give the zloty room [[n1256]], yet Bankier's currency survey finds analysts unconvinced by an 'era of a strong zloty' [[n1428]]. Credit is re-accelerating: mortgage sales are sharply higher on 'government steroids', a quarter 'like the good old days' [[n1462]], which feeds bank volumes but also housing demand.
Fiscal & Politics

Politics is in an awkward interregnum that markets are choosing to look through. OKO.press calls the newly sworn Morawiecki cabinet a government for two weeks that will fall after 14 days [[n1435]], and Gazeta Prawna says it has no chance of a confidence vote and no budget [[n1417]]. The 2024 budget that matters will instead be submitted by Donald Tusk's government [[n1305]], so the fiscal plan investors must price is the new coalition's, whose full cabinet list is already circulating [[n1356]]. The fiscal prize is EU money: the European Commission accepted Poland's revised KPO recovery plan, with energy the biggest winner [[n1244]]. Tusk's flagship pledge to raise pay [[n1309]] is the spending risk bond investors will price once the new team takes office; a pay rise funded by EU inflows is benign, one funded by extra issuance is not.
Corporate & Sectors

The KPO approval, with energy named the biggest winner, coincides with a sharp utility rally: PGE is +16.90% over five sessions at 8.45 PLN and Tauron +12.65% at 4.23 PLN. PGE also adds a nuclear leg, as PGE PAK Energia Jądrowa received the decision-in-principle for a KHNP plant in Wielkopolska [[n1422]]. CD Projekt earned over 200 mln zł of net profit in Q3 [[n1454]], yet the stock closed -1.51% at 107.95 PLN and is -4.64% over five sessions, so the print lands on a share that has been de-rating into it. Budimex won a Czech D11 motorway contract worth 2 mld zł [[n1234]], a sign that Polish contractors can export capacity while domestic tenders wait for EU money. Retail is split, with Pepco +30.36% over 20 sessions and Dino +13.79% at 444.00 PLN while Allegro is -2.20%, so the consumer recovery is being priced in discount and food retail rather than in e-commerce. JSW is the casualty at -18.27% over five sessions, with Wyborcza reporting that prosecutors slowed a probe into money siphoned out of the coal miner [[n1319]].
Geopolitics & Security

Security spending is structural, not cyclical. Rzeczpospolita reports Poland is building an air shield worth 54 mld zł that will also protect its Patriot batteries [[n1424]]. The threat is concrete: Poland charged 16 people after dismantling a Russian spy ring [[n1174]], evidence that the war's spillover risk now extends inside Poland's borders. The Ukrainian relationship also carries economic friction, as Polish truckers started a round-the-clock blockade of a fourth border crossing [[n1192]]. For investors the blockade is a logistics and trade-flow risk for exporters and transport names, while defence outlays are a multi-year commitment that a change of government is unlikely to reverse.
New / Most Important

The NBP has become a political battleground. A new NBP banner no longer argues that inflation is gone; it now says Governor Glapiński is 'the best' [[n1467]]. Rzeczpospolita reports the NBP pays millions to Glapiński's advisers and will not disclose their names [[n1415]], the kind of disclosure fight that invites scrutiny from the incoming coalition. The bank is also publicly rebutting accusations that its bond purchases were unconstitutional [[n1307]], a defence suggesting the bank expects scrutiny under a new government. For markets the risk is credibility rather than the policy rate: a central bank in open conflict with the incoming government can widen the risk premium on Polish bonds and the currency even as the fundamentals improve.
Playbook ✓

Stay long Polish equities through EPOL and the WIG20TR tracker, overweight banks (PKO, Pekao, mBank) and KPO-linked utilities (PGE, Tauron), sized for headline volatility around the NBP and for legal risk after the Supreme Court voided a loan agreement over a bank's FX tables [[n1352]]. Trigger to add: a clean confidence vote for the Tusk cabinet and a 2024 budget that funds the pay pledge without a jump in issuance. What changes the call: a confrontation that threatens NBP independence or a stall in KPO disbursement. ⚠ Divergence: the macro and currency signals are unambiguously positive, but the institutions are in open conflict, with a caretaker cabinet lacking a majority and a central bank campaigning for its own governor, so the political risk premium could rise just as growth improves.
Narrative

Platform software is carrying the AI trade while hardware gets scrutinised. XLK closed at 184.75 USD, +13.45% over 20 sessions but -0.38% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Microsoft is +13.46% and Adobe +18.29% over the same 20 sessions, while Apple trails at 190.40 USD.
Reported

HPE projected sales that fall short of estimates on server demand [[n0696]], a reminder that the AI build-out is not lifting every hardware vendor, as budgets appear to shift from general-purpose servers to accelerators. Apple is trying to unwind its Goldman Sachs credit-card partnership [[n0649]], trimming a low-margin financial-services experiment rather than adding one.
EPS Upside Watch

Cloud distribution is widening: Amazon will offer Salesforce apps on AWS, allowing easier integration of AI tech [[n0519]]. Marketplaces that bundle software with compute shorten sales cycles, which is where upside to 2024 software revenue estimates is most likely to appear, especially for vendors whose pricing scales with usage rather than seats.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Consensus treats AI as a chip story; the better risk-reward now sits in software with usage-based pricing, where server-cycle shortfalls like HPE's do not bite. Stay Bullish, but fund it from hardware rather than adding net exposure while the sector consolidates its 20-session gain.

Communication services have rallied on lower yields, but the news flow is about liability, not growth. XLC closed at 70.69 USD, +9.78% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Meta is +12.00%, Alphabet +10.24% and Netflix +16.81%, while Disney fell -2.81% in Tuesday's session.
Reported

EPS Upside Watch

Advertising budgets leaving X have to land somewhere, and the largest, most measurable platforms tend to capture them; that is the near-term upside case for Meta and Alphabet ad revenue into the holiday quarter. Netflix's +16.81% month shows investors still pay for subscription pricing power.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The market prices regulatory risk at Meta as a fine-sized cost. The underappreciated threat is product redesign: if child-safety litigation forces changes to recommendation algorithms, engagement and ad load fall together, and that hits margins far harder than any settlement. Mixed until the legal path clarifies.
Narrative

Financials are the cleanest beneficiary of a soft landing with lower long yields. XLF closed at 35.25 USD, +10.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Bank of America is +14.95%, JPMorgan +11.73%, and the regional-bank KRE +11.81% despite a -2.33% five-session pullback.
Reported

Bank of America pays a $12 mln fine for misreporting mortgage data [[n0653]], a cost of doing business rather than a franchise risk. Its +14.95% month suggests investors care far more about the securities book than about conduct fines of that size.
EPS Upside Watch

Consolidation is the upside catalyst: KBW has named the regional banks at greatest risk of being taken over by rivals [[n1631]]. Takeover premia matter because acquirers with excess capital can buy deposit franchises below replacement cost when regional valuations are depressed, and the bid itself re-rates the rest of the group.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Investors still treat falling yields as bad for bank margins. For banks carrying underwater securities, lower long yields shrink unrealised losses and free capital faster than they compress net interest income. Stay Bullish, with large money-centre names ahead of regionals.
Narrative

Energy is the one sector that has gone nowhere, -0.31% over 20 sessions at 84.65 USD for XLE (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28), because crude has slid: Brent sits at 81.68 USD/bbl, -6.56% over 20 sessions, WTI at 76.41 USD/bbl, -7.17%, and Henry Hub gas -24.31% to 2.71 USD/MMBtu.
Reported

EPS Upside Watch

Downstream and gas exposure are the swing factors for estimates. Exxon is -1.87% over 20 sessions and SLB -7.25%, so services already discount weaker activity; integrated majors with refining and chemicals can hold earnings even if crude stays near current levels, while gas-weighted producers face estimate cuts after the month's collapse.

Consensus frames the OPEC decision as binary. The bigger signal is natural gas: a -24.31% month is disinflation that helps consumers and industrial users more than it hurts the integrated majors. Mixed, with a bias to integrated balance sheets over pure upstream.

Widebody demand supports engine and aftermarket earnings well into 2024, which is where estimate revisions tend to follow; Boeing's +21.95% month says the market is starting to price that recovery.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Investors still price industrials off the manufacturing PMI. The better guide is backlog quality: aerospace backlogs are long-dated and price-protected, while ag equipment is exposed to farm incomes. Stay Bullish on aerospace, avoid machinery tied to the farm cycle until dealer inventories and order books stabilise.

Consumer discretionary has priced a strong holiday. XLY closed at 169.48 USD, +12.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Amazon is +10.79% and Home Depot +11.32%, while Lululemon slipped -1.82% in Tuesday's session. Reported

Cyber Monday sales hit a record $12.4 billion even as savings dwindle [[n0146]], and Amazon called its Black Friday and Cyber Monday event its 'biggest ever' [[n0143]]. Headline volumes are strong, but the savings cushion behind them is thinning, which makes them harder to repeat.
EPS Upside Watch

Scale is the margin lever: the biggest platforms can fund promotions from advertising and logistics income, while specialty retailers fund them from gross margin. That asymmetry is where fourth-quarter EPS surprises will separate, favouring Amazon over discount-dependent chains.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The market reads record holiday spending as bullish. The more relevant number is margin: promotional intensity transfers value from retailers to shoppers. Favour scale platforms over discount-dependent specialty retail, and watch full-price brands such as Nike and Lululemon as the test of that thesis. Mixed for the sector as a whole.

EPS Upside Watch

Pricing power is fading as goods inflation cools, so volume has to do the work. The upside case is value retail: warehouse clubs gain share as shoppers trade down, consistent with Costco outpacing Walmart over the month. Branded food faces the opposite mix, with slowing price increases and a structural volume question from appetite-suppressing drugs.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The consensus treats GLP-1 drugs as a niche risk for snacks. If adoption broadens, the volume hit spreads to beverages and packaged food, and defensive multiples no longer look defensive. Mixed, with a preference for value retail over branded food.
Narrative

Health care is the laggard of the rally, XLV +4.69% over 20 sessions at 129.64 USD and -0.51% on Tuesday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28). Eli Lilly is at 591.60 USD, Novo Nordisk's ADR fell -2.35%, and Pfizer is -2.82% over 20 sessions, while Intuitive Surgical is +20.29%.
Reported

A data analysis found Lilly's Mounjaro leads to more and faster weight loss than Novo's obesity drug [[n1619]]. The FDA is investigating the safety risk of CAR-T cancer therapies [[n0762]], a regulatory overhang for cell-therapy developers.
EPS Upside Watch

Obesity remains the clearest estimate-revision story in large-cap pharma: head-to-head efficacy data shift prescribing at the margin, and supply capacity determines who captures the demand. Lilly's ability to convert its efficacy edge into volume is the upside case, while post-Covid franchises like Pfizer keep resetting lower.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Investors still treat pharma as one defensive block. The real trade is dispersion: obesity leaders versus post-Covid decliners, and device makers such as Intuitive Surgical, whose +20.29% month suggests procedure volumes are holding up. Mixed for the sector, Bullish on obesity share-gainers and cautious on Covid-exposed franchises.

Materials are turning on a weaker dollar and steadier metals. Reported

The Northern Miner expects gold and silver to rise as political and economic risks grind on [[n0114]], and the tape agrees: Freeport-McMoRan rose +1.72% on Tuesday and the copper-miner ETF COPX +2.15%, while Alcoa slipped -0.84%, so the bid favours copper and gold over aluminium.
EPS Upside Watch

Silver's +5.73% over five sessions shows the precious-metals bid is broadening beyond gold. With gold at 2,040.00 USD/oz, producers' margins expand faster than revenues because mining costs are largely fixed, which is where EPS upside sits for the next reporting season; Newmont's +6.26% session on Tuesday shows how quickly that leverage is being priced.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Consensus wants Chinese stimulus before owning materials. The faster driver is the dollar: a DXY at 102.75, down -3.18% over 20 sessions, lifts dollar-priced commodities regardless of Chinese demand. Bullish, led by precious-metal producers rather than base metals.

Data centers are the earnings upside: full-campus leases convert to long-dated contracted rent, and power-constrained supply supports pricing. Logistics and student housing, the other assets on Blackstone's list, share the same feature of structural demand that does not depend on the office cycle.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Investors treat REITs as a pure duration trade. The more durable story is asset mix: digital and logistics landlords grow rents even if yields stall, while office owners need lower rates just to stand still. Stay Bullish, favouring data center and industrial REITs over office.

Utilities have lagged the rally despite falling yields. XLU closed at 62.99 USD, +1.43% over five sessions and +6.44% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28); Constellation Energy is +10.10% and NextEra +1.68% over 20 sessions.

Data center load is the upside driver for generators with firm, clean capacity, consistent with Constellation's outperformance over NextEra. Regulated utilities face the opposite problem: capital spending to connect that load must be approved by regulators before it earns a return.

The market treats utilities as bond proxies. The more relevant split is between regulated wires and merchant generators selling to data centers. Mixed overall, as the bond-proxy bid fades whenever yields stabilise, with a preference for existing nuclear fleets over small modular reactor developers.

Cost-cutting is the only near-term EPS lever, and headcount reduction can lift margins in 2024 even with flat volumes, but restructuring charges arrive first. Huawei's push into EVs with new cars and automaker partnerships adds another well-funded Chinese competitor [[n0232]], pressuring pricing in the market that used to fund European margins.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Consensus sees European autos as cheap. Cheap is the problem: the margin base is being eroded by Chinese cost competition. Bearish on volume brands; selective on premium names with pricing power, such as BMW, whose +6.31% month shows investors already make that distinction.

earnings_pattern.title: Margins beat volumes; guidance is the verdict
parts: Rewarded

Investors are paying for credible forward guidance and margin control. easyJet's better-than-expected results sent its share price flying [[n1638]], proof that the rule holds outside retail as leisure demand turns into profit, and Abercrombie & Fitch raised its outlook after quarterly sales surged 20% [[n0848]]. Target shares jumped more than 17% after a big earnings beat even as sales fell again [[n0831]]: the market rewarded the profit line and inventory discipline, not the top line. Each gave investors a reason to revisit next year's numbers, not just this quarter's.
Punished

Weak guidance is being sold regardless of the quarter. Deere tumbled after its 2024 guidance missed estimates [[n0264]] and is -5.34% over five sessions, and HPE's projection of sales short of estimates on server demand [[n0696]] puts AI-adjacent hardware to the same test. Guidance misses can be punished harder than beats are rewarded, because a lower 2024 base resets every multiple applied to it. Even Nvidia's record third quarter [[n0855]] has not prevented a -5.13% five-session decline (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-28), proof that a beat priced in advance is not a catalyst.
Pattern

The common thread is that margins beat volumes. Target was rewarded for profit delivery on falling sales, while Deere was punished for what next year looks like, and HPE now faces the same verdict. In a disinflationary tape, companies that cut inventory and protect gross margin get re-rated, while those dependent on a cyclical volume rebound are discounted until the rebound is visible. Nvidia is the extreme case: revenue up 200% year-on-year [[n0873]] was not enough to lift the stock, because the bar had already moved with the share price. Expect that rule to hold until volumes re-accelerate.
Attention into EPS

Holiday trading is the next earnings input, and the mix matters more than the record headlines. Record Cyber Monday spending arrived even as savings dwindle [[n0146]], which supports fourth-quarter revenue but signals that promotional intensity will weigh on retail gross margins. Investors are likely to reward retailers that held price and punish those that bought volume with markdowns.
Playbook

Buy margin-led beats on the first pullback after the print, and avoid companies whose 2024 guidance depends on a cyclical volume recovery, from farm equipment to servers. Trigger: guidance revisions in the next reporting wave, especially from retailers reporting holiday-quarter margins. What changes the call: a re-acceleration in volumes that rewards operating leverage over cost discipline.

GDX and Newmont give leveraged exposure to the metal, because costs are largely fixed while revenue moves with price. The risk is that leverage cuts both ways, and energy and labour cost inflation can absorb margin gains.
Trigger to Watch
A further DXY decline below 102.75 alongside falling real yields; reverse if gold slips back under the $2,000 level it broke below in the earlier dollar bounce [[n1741]].

underowned.title: Uranium: the quiet commodity bull

Cameco and URA offer fuel-cycle exposure without reactor-construction risk; URA spreads the bet across miners and fuel processors such as Centrus Energy, +2.00% over 20 sessions. New reactor decisions, such as the decision-in-principle for PGE PAK's planned plant in Poland [[n1422]], and long-term utility contracting; reverse on a supply response that caps prices.

underowned.title: Long Treasuries nobody wants

Semafor declares that 'nobody wants U.S. Treasury bonds' [[n1825]], while household cash keeps flowing into money-market funds and CDs instead [[n1063]]. TLT carries the most duration per dollar and benefits most if growth slows. Money-market cash rotating out of bills as cut expectations firm; reverse if the 10Y climbs back toward 4.88%. Core portfolios keep the intermediate-duration stance in IEF, with TLT as the satellite expression.

parts: Attention Gap

EMB gives diversified sovereign spread plus duration in one instrument, and issuers that hiked early now have real-rate room to ease. The risk is idiosyncratic: a single large sovereign restructuring can dent returns, and a dollar rebound hits both spreads and local fundamentals.
Trigger to Watch
A weaker dollar and falling US yields together, the combination of the past month; reverse if DXY recovers toward 106.12, its level 20 sessions ago.

crypto.title: Bitcoin consolidates while the ETF plumbing improves
parts: Market Context
